description:
FILED s529b (Opus, 2026-10-31) while doing #3856 (its RULED section: "`use re '/x'` is a SECOND SOURCE of the flag ... if PCL does not track it, FILE that as its own task (engine + scanner together)").  PRE-EXISTING (main d8577478).  PCL tracks only `use re 'eval'` (Parser2 _re_eval_in_scope); the `/FLAGS` form (perl 5.14+, re.pm: `use re '/flags'` sets the default modifiers for every pattern compiled in the lexical scope) is not read at all.

PROBE (scratch/s529b/re1.pl, perl 5.40.3 vs the s529b tree):
    { use re "/x"; print "a ", ("q" =~ /q # c
    / ? "ok" : "no"), "\n"; }
    { use re "/i"; print "b ", ("Q" =~ /q/ ? "ok" : "no"), "\n"; }
    { use re "/x"; my $nl = "\nZ"; print "c ", ("q" =~ /q # $nl
    / ? "ok" : "no"), "\n"; }
  perl: a ok / b ok / c ok        PCL: a no / b no / c no
Row c is the scanner half (#3856's p3856c row 21, left out of Pl/t/regex-x-comment-01.t for this reason): with the flag known, Pl::InterpScan::scan's `x => 1` already skips the comment.

FIX SHAPE (suggested): the compiler tracks the pragma's flag set lexically (the _re_eval_in_scope walk is the shape, or the lexical-pragma machinery strict/feature use) and ORs it into each literal's `:flags` at compile time (m//, qr//, s///, split's pattern) -- perl applies it at the pattern's compile, so a run-time interpolated pattern takes the flags of its OP's scope; the same set feeds `x => ...` for the scanner.  `use re '/u'` / `'/a'` / `'/aa'` / `'/l'` / `'/d'` (charset) and `'/xx'` / `'/n'` / `'/m'` / `'/s'` belong to the same mechanism; `no re '/x'` turns one off.


=== DONE (s530c) ===
FIXED.  ONE scope walk `Pl::Parser2::re_pragma_at` (the `use re 'eval'` walk, now shared: `_re_eval_in_scope` is a one-line reader of it) applies every preceding `use re` / `no re` statement in source order from the document inward, with re.pm bits()'s rules (letters on/off, second x = xx, second a = aa, exclusive charset, `no re` with no argument = all off); a per-document flag answers the common no-`re` case after one parent walk.  `re_merge_default_flags` ORs the defaults into a literal's own letters (an explicit charset on the literal replaces the default one).  Consumers: ExprToCL `_regex_literal_form` (m// qr// split) BEFORE its /x reading -- so the #3856 scanner option `x => 1` follows a pragma /x with no extra code -- and `gen_substitution_form` (a copy of PPI's modifier hash); a RUN-TIME pattern operand of `=~` / `!~` (perl compiles it with the op's defaults: `use re '/i'; "q" =~ $p` matches) becomes `(p-regex-from-parts :pat RHS :flags DEF)` only when the pragma is in force (a qr operand keeps its own flags there).
Guard Pl/t/re-pragma-flags-01.t (28 rows; the filing's three rows a/b/c, no re, qr stringification, s///, run-time and interpolated patterns, split, /s /m /xx, lexical-not-dynamic, inner `no re`, qw(/i /s), !~, qr operand) -- inverse-verified: 17 of 28 FAIL on a 0fb05a79 extraction.  corpus-diff vs 0fb05a79: IDENTICAL over 111 files (no `use re '/..'` in the corpus).  ir-spec §10-reflags; docs/interp-scan.md contract line.
Residue FILED #4101: a string eval inside the scope does not inherit the defaults (perl: it does).
subject: SILENT WRONG: `use re '/x'` / `'/i'` / any `use re '/FLAGS'` default-modifier pragma is ignored -- the lexically scoped default flags never reach a pattern (engine) nor the interpolation scanner (#3856's second source of the /x flag)
